speaker: Thorfinn
text: For a long time, I let anger and revenge control every breath I took.

speaker: Zeno of Citium
text: You suffered because you tied your soul to things outside your control.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: I see that now. True freedom is mastering my own hands, not the world around me.

speaker: Zeno of Citium
text: Precisely. When reason governs your reactions, no external force can conquer your tranquility.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Can a man who lived only for murder ever truly become a man of peace?

speaker: Heraclitus
text: No man steps in the same river twice. You are not the man you were.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: But the blood I spilled is still part of the river. It shaped who I am.

speaker: Heraclitus
text: The tension of opposites sustains the world. Your past violence makes your present peace meaningful.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: How do you build a quiet life after tearing down so many others?

speaker: Pythagoras
text: By discovering the natural proportions of the soul. Chaos must be ordered by strict discipline.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Discipline is harder than fighting. It means holding still when everything tells you to strike.

speaker: Pythagoras
text: That restraint is the highest mathematics. Harmony is achieved when the chaotic mind finds its balance.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: I know how to fight, but I have decided to drop my sword.

speaker: Miyamoto Musashi
text: To know the sword and keep it sheathed requires a spirit as unmoving as a mountain.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Is true strength winning the battle, or killing the desire to fight at all?

speaker: Miyamoto Musashi
text: The ultimate aim of martial arts is not having to use them. You have found the true Way.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: I used to think I knew exactly what justice was. Now, I realize I know nothing.

speaker: Socrates
text: Does realizing your own ignorance make you feel lost, or does it set you free?

speaker: Thorfinn
text: It terrifies me. I don't even know if I truly understand what a good person is.

speaker: Socrates
text: That very terror is the beginning of wisdom. Only those who question can ever find the good.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: We are trying to build a land without war, but people carry their greed with them.

speaker: Plato
text: A society is merely the human soul written in large letters. It reflects its citizens.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Then we cannot just pretend to be peaceful. We have to actually change inside.

speaker: Plato
text: Exactly. True justice is an invisible harmony within, not merely an outward appearance of order.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Choosing peace wasn't just one decision. It's something I have to force myself to do daily.

speaker: Aristotle
text: Virtue is not a singular act, but a habit. We become just by doing just actions.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Good intentions mean nothing if I still raise my fists when I get angry.

speaker: Aristotle
text: Practical wisdom requires constant repetition. You are reshaping your character through every restrained breath.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Sometimes I think I must walk through suffering to protect the people I love.

speaker: Epicurus
text: Is it truly wise to invite suffering when a quiet, obscure life offers untroubled peace?

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Avoiding pain won't build a new world. Some burdens are worth carrying.

speaker: Epicurus
text: Perhaps, as long as you do not mistake unnecessary hardship for noble virtue.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Kings and lords cause so much death just to hoard gold and land.

speaker: Diogenes of Sinope
text: They are fools chasing shadows! A man only needs a cloak, a bowl, and the sun.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: I want to build a village where people can farm and live together without that greed.

speaker: Diogenes of Sinope
text: You trade a king's madness for a farmer's worry. True peace means needing nothing at all.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Can we ever justify hurting a few people if it means bringing peace to many?

speaker: John Stuart Mill
text: The greatest happiness for the greatest number is the foundation of all true morality.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: But if we force individuals to suffer for the majority, aren't we just tyrants?

speaker: John Stuart Mill
text: That is why individual liberty is sacred. You cannot build a just society by crushing the individual.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: If I fight only to protect my friends, does my good intention make the violence right?

speaker: Immanuel Kant
text: No. You cannot use immoral means to achieve a moral end.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: But if I do nothing, innocent people will be killed. I have to protect them.

speaker: Immanuel Kant
text: You must protect them, but you must never treat any human being merely as a tool.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: You cannot build a lasting peace on a foundation of manipulation and bloodshed.

speaker: Lelouch vi Britannia
text: Sometimes someone must gather all the world's hatred onto themselves to break the cycle of violence.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: But playing god with people's lives only creates a different kind of nightmare.

speaker: Lelouch vi Britannia
text: I destroyed the old world to create a new one. True peace always requires a sacrifice.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Carrying all the suffering by yourself doesn't save the people you leave behind.

speaker: Itachi Uchiha
text: I chose the shadows so my brother could walk in the light. It was my duty.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Peace built on a mountain of hidden bodies is just a lie waiting to break.

speaker: Itachi Uchiha
text: Perhaps you are right. A true leader must trust others to share the burden.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Am I truly a peaceful man, or am I just using this life to escape my past?

speaker: Jean-Paul Sartre
text: You are nothing but the sum of your choices. There is no hidden, fixed nature inside you.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Then I must prove who I am every single day, with every choice I make.

speaker: Jean-Paul Sartre
text: Yes. You are condemned to be free. The burden of creating your identity is entirely yours.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Believing in peace is easy, but making the sacrifices to live it is terrifying.

speaker: Søren Kierkegaard
text: That terror is the dizziness of freedom. A genuine commitment requires a leap into the unknown.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: I know how difficult the path is, but I will walk it anyway.

speaker: Søren Kierkegaard
text: Then you act with true, passionate inwardness. You have stopped observing life and started living it.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: I have the power to destroy my enemies, but true strength is choosing not to.

speaker: Friedrich Nietzsche
text: Are you sure this 'peace' isn't just the exhaustion of a warrior afraid of his own shadow?

speaker: Thorfinn
text: It takes more strength to absorb a blow without striking back than it does to kill.

speaker: Friedrich Nietzsche
text: If it is born of overcoming your own impulses, then it is a profound will to power.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Living only to fight the darkness will eventually leave you hollow inside.

speaker: Guts
text: When the world marks you for death, swinging the sword is the only way to breathe.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: I understand that pain. But fighting a war with no end is just another kind of prison.

speaker: Guts
text: I don't care about prisons or peace. I just endure, no matter what it takes.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Stealing freedom from the rest of the world isn't true freedom at all.

speaker: Eren Yeager
text: If someone tries to take my freedom, I won't hesitate to take theirs first.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: That only spreads the cycle of hatred. You become the very monster you hated.

speaker: Eren Yeager
text: I just keep moving forward. Until my enemies are destroyed, nothing else matters.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Is there any point in building a peaceful village if death and suffering will always find us?

speaker: Albert Camus
text: The universe remains silent to our pleas. But we must stubbornly revolt against that indifference.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: So we just keep trying to build a better life, even knowing it might not last?

speaker: Albert Camus
text: Yes. The struggle itself toward the heights is enough to fill a man's heart.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: No matter how hollow you feel inside, I will not let you destroy innocent lives.

speaker: Johan Liebert
text: But look at them. Strip away their fragile rules, and you will see there is nothing inside them either.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: People are not empty. They suffer, they love, and they try to build something better.

speaker: Johan Liebert
text: The end of everything is simply oblivion. We are all equal only in death.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: You do not create justice by appointing yourself the judge and executioner of the world.

speaker: Light Yagami
text: Someone has to pull the weeds. I am the only one with the will to eradicate the rot.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: When you put yourself above everyone else, you are just a murderer with delusions.

speaker: Light Yagami
text: I am not a murderer. I am the god of the new, peaceful world you claim to want.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: I killed because I refused to think. I just followed the orders of men I hated.

speaker: Hannah Arendt
text: That thoughtlessness is the root of the greatest terrors. Evil relies on blind obedience.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: Refusing to question your own actions can be just as dangerous as deliberately choosing evil.

speaker: Hannah Arendt
text: Precisely. Personal responsibility means you can never surrender your independent judgment to authority.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: I try to look at the people I've hurt and genuinely understand the pain I caused them.

speaker: Simone Weil
text: To truly see another's affliction without turning away requires a complete emptying of yourself.

speaker: Thorfinn
text: It hurts to look at what I've done, but looking away feels like another act of violence.

speaker: Simone Weil
text: Absolutely unmixed attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity we can offer the wounded.
